body.text:
“Alpha Charles wishes you a Merry Christmas. This is your gift.”
On Christmas Day, a package arrived—sent by my mate.
Inside were twelve roses, a Pandora bracelet, and a piece of Victoria’s Secret lingerie.
I almost smiled. After years of marriage and ruling a pack together, he still bothered with these rehearsed gestures of romance.
But when my eyes fell on the card, I froze.
*Dear Alison, Merry Christmas.*
“You’ve delivered this to the wrong person,” I said calmly.
I took the clipboard from the courier, wrote down the correct address—Alpha Charles’s young assistant, Alison Dickson.
“And take this with you as well,” I added, placing a sealed envelope in his hands. “Give it directly to Alpha Charles.”
The courier nodded.
Inside was the divorce agreement I had prepared long ago.
--
Two hours later, Alpha Charles came home.
Tulips in one hand, a box of donuts in the other.
He took off his coat, waited for the warmth to return to his body, then stepped behind me and wrapped his arms around my waist.
“Your favorite flowers,” he murmured.
“And donuts—we ate them every day when we first started dating. They’re practically our love token.”
“Crowds were insane for Christmas. I waited in line forever to buy these. Come on, try one.”
I held the donut in my hands.
I had been craving it for two months, and today I finally got one, yet somehow, the taste was bitter.
It lodged in my throat, impossible to swallow.
“Why aren’t you with her?” I asked, casually tossing the donut straight into the trash.
Alpha Charles froze. “What?”
“Didn’t you say you were on a business trip and wouldn’t be home for days? I was sick and needed to go to the hospital, and you wouldn’t even come back. But the moment Alison needs company for Christmas, suddenly you appear.”
“How long are you planning to lie to me?”
The words poured out, years of swallowed grievances finally breaking loose and cracking through the fading mate bond.
“Alison just broke up. She’s upset, and I thought—”
“Her being upset is none of your damn business!” I shouted at him.
Alpha Charles pressed his lips together, his brow tightening.
“She’s just a young girl. Why are you competing with her? I’m only her Alpha.”
A bitter smile tugged at my lips.
“Her boss buys his secretary Victoria’s Secret sleepwear? Planning to comfort her all the way into your bed?”
He reacted like a cat whose tail had been stepped on—
anger exploding in an instant.
He hurled the tulips to the floor, smashing them violently.
Petals flew everywhere, and a broken stem whipped across my shin, slicing my skin open.
A hot, stinging pain spread across my leg.
“Do you think this is funny?! How many times have I explained it? There’s nothing going on between me and her,” he demanded.
I lifted my eyes and looked at his enraged, twisted face, suddenly feeling as if he were a complete stranger.
“No,” I said softly.
“Charles, these six years… haven’t been funny at all.”
That night, we slept in separate rooms.
The guest room light stayed on until dawn.
He was video-calling Alison.
Singing Christmas songs together, sharing little moments from their day, listening to her mindless complaints.
“You broke your promise. I won’t forgive you,” she pouted.
Alpha Charles soothed her gently. “Be good. I’ll make it up to you tomorrow.”
“Did you hang your stocking? I’ll come by tomorrow night with your present… Do I really have to wear the Santa suit…? Fine.”
The moment she acted coy, he caved.
I stood outside the door.
My heart clenched as I thought of our never-once-celebrated anniversary.
My nose burned, breath catching painfully in my chest.
I couldn’t breathe.
When I woke up, Alpha Charles had already made breakfast.
He moved around the dining table as if nothing had happened—placing a fried egg into my plate, setting a warm glass of milk beside me, playing the role of the gentle mate he used to be.
“I’ll go with you to the hospital in a bit…” he began.
His phone rang.
On the screen were just two letters: AD.
The ringtone wasn’t one he ever used around me—clearly one set just for her.
Alpha Charles stepped into the kitchen to take the call.
Moments later, he came out already changing his clothes, slipping into his shoes,
the warmth of moments ago evaporating like mist.
“Something came up. I’ll have the driver take you.”
“I’ll transfer you some money later. It’s winter—buy a few new coats.”
Under normal circumstances, I would have questioned him until he slipped, until he faltered and the truth cracked through.
But today… maybe I had been dismissed too many times, or maybe I simply no longer cared to compete with Alison.
I didn’t say a single word.
He left.
I went to the hospital alone.
While waiting for the test results, I opened Instagram and saw Alison’s newest post: “Stupid cat, you scared me to death.”
In the photo, she sat in the passenger seat of Alpha Charles’s G-Wagon—leaning against my soft pillow, wrapped in my blanket.
Her ragdoll cat perched on her lap.
From the side of the frame, a familiar hand—long, well-boned, unmistakably Alpha Charles’s—reached over.
I couldn’t tell whether he was petting the cat or tugging down her too-short skirt.
“Found his mouth red this morning. I thought it was blood and nearly cried myself sick. Turns out he stole cranberries.”
Comments flooded beneath: 
“Someone else panicked more than you. He can’t stand to hear you cry. Didn’t he run a red light for you last time and get pulled over? Admit it already, Charles~”
“Oh, wasn’t that Valentine’s Day? Snowstorm so heavy you couldn’t see the road. Our Luna rushed to the precinct in a camisole to bail him out—shivering blue from the cold—still not knowing he lost control because of Alison. You two hide things well.”
Tears splattered across my screen, breaking into blurred patches.
Alpha Charles had lied to me.
Back then, the serial-killer case had the whole city on edge.
He told me he ran the red light because he was terrified something had happened to me.
But he had been racing to protect Alison.
I stared at the photo for a long time.
Open bags of chips, half-finished milk tea…
Alpha Charles had severe cleanliness rules—no food allowed in his car, not even from me.
Yet for her, he broke every boundary.
I was so dazed I didn’t notice the nurse until she tapped my shoulder.
“Luna Melissa, your results are out.”
“You’re pregnant.”
I held the report, a laugh bubbling up but breaking into uncontrollable tears instead.
After a long moment, I dialed Alpha Charles.
“Come to the hospital.”
In the background, I heard a girl’s laughter.
“Are you really sick?” he asked, suddenly tense. “What did the doctor say?”
“I…”
“Charles, the bath is ready. Come in,”
Alison’s voice chimed sweetly.
The line went dead silent.
My hand shook violently.
My blood felt like it was crystallizing into ice.
“What… what are you two doing?”
The phone slipped from my fingers, shattering against the floor—shattering everything with it.
I doubled over and vomited violently.
It felt like a giant hand was wrenching my insides—my heart, my stomach, my skull pounding until my vision went white.
I hit the floor hard.
When awareness flickered again, I was on a hospital bed in the emergency room.
The doctor was saying they needed to contact my family.
“No… don’t…”
I dug my nails into my palm until they nearly broke skin, forcing the words out.
“Doctor… remove it. I don’t want the baby.”
“I don’t want anything anymore.”
By the time I got home, it was deep into the night.
The house was empty.
I went into the bathroom and stayed under the hot water for a long, long time before my body finally stopped shaking.
In the fogged-up mirror, I touched my lower abdomen gently.
There had been a life there once.
Now there was only a hollow ache.
I forced myself out of the grief.
After showering, I treated my frostbitten hands and feet, took down the wedding photos, and cleared away every object tied to a beautiful memory.
Each thing I threw out made my heart tremble, and strengthened my resolve to leave.
Because I had seen how much Alpha Charles once loved me, his change now cut like a spear, like a blade, slicing through me from the outside all the way in.
I bled in ways he would never see.
Before I knew it, it was three in the morning.
I booked a morning flight and placed the divorce agreement and the abortion record neatly on the dining table.
If he came home, he would see them.

body.text:
“Vanessa!” her mother yelled. “Vanessa, are you here?”

The crowd thundered down the wooden steps like a herd of wild beasts. The wooden steps creaked as they bore the weight of the concerned adults rushing into the musty darkness.

“Were you playing in the crawlspace?” Charlie’s dad asked. “I told you kids to stay out of the crawlspace.”

Charlie’s dad pulled the draw string from an overhead light. The soft orange glow of the incandescent bulb illuminated the basement. Stacks of cardboard boxes and other plastic containers littered the space like castle walls. A bench in the corner scattered with an assortment of tools and other items for menial home repairs. Christmas, Halloween, and other holiday decorations packed into a corner waited for their seasons. The hint of mildew permeated the air.

“Vanessa,” her mother called out. “Vanessa, this isn’t funny.”

“Vanessa. Get out here right now or you’re grounded for a week,” her father yelled.

The adults scattered to the four corners of the basement searching for her.

A pair of feet thundered down the steps. “Loser, what did you do now?” a voice asked.

Charlie turned and glared at his sister, Julie, standing near the end of the basement steps, still wearing the sweatpants and T-shirt from her volleyball practice.

“Julie, this isn’t the time,” Charlie’s mom said. She pointed a finger at her—the universal parental sign to knock it off. “Go back upstairs.”

“Fine,” she said as she stomped her way back upstairs.

“Get the flashlight from the workbench,” Charlie’s dad said. “I think I see something in the crawlspace.”

“Here. Use mine,” Officer Ron said as he rushed to join Charlie’s father. He shone the light into the small space above the cinderblocks on the back side of the basement.

“I don’t see her,” Officer Ron said. “I don’t see anything. Wait . . . maybe something back there. Here, give me a hand.”

The other adults tore into the boxes and plastic containers. They searched under every nook and cranny of the basement. They searched a few cabinets that had been placed down there.

Nothing. They found nothing.

“Where is she, Charlie?” his mother asked.

Charlie’s eyes locked onto her real location. Where she was hidden. Where she was trapped.

Next to an old storage cabinet was the oval-shaped full-length mirror carved into a dark mahogany wood. A radiant sun dial was in the wood above the mirror. Two wooden legs kept it upright. This was their secret. Their secret place for adventure. For fun. And now everyone must know.

Charlie’s mom approached him. She placed her hands on his shoulders. “Charlie, you need to tell us right now,” his mother said. “Where is Vanessa hiding down here?”

Charlie gulped. “Promise I won’t get in trouble?”

“I promise you. You won’t be in trouble.”

Charlie pointed to the mirror and said, “She’s in there.”

“She’s in where?” Vanessa’s mother asked.

“She’s in the mirror,” Charlie said.

“Charlie, this isn’t one of your silly games or stories,” his mother said. “This is serious.”

Tears welled in Charlie’s eyes. “I’m serious, Mom,” he said. “I need you to believe me.”

“Charlie, tell the truth,” his father said in a stern voice. “Where is she?”

“She’s in the mirror!” Charlie yelled. “And I can’t get to her.”

“What is he talking about?” Vanessa’s dad asked.

Charlie rushed over to the mirror. “She’s in here,” he proclaimed. “Nessa is in the mirror. We can travel through this mirror to a magical realm. It has castles and knights and magic. Turning this dial activates the mirror.”

Charlie turned the sun dial clockwise and counterclockwise a series of times.

“When I do that, it should open, and we can pass through. We’ve been going there for years. Years. Since we were like five. We were supposed to go through today after school. But I had my doctor’s appointment. She must have gone through before I got home.” His words trailed off. Tears fell down his face.

He continued, “Now, I can’t get it to work again, and she’s trapped inside.”

Silence fell over the basement. The five adults stood in stunned silence. It could have been a moment, an hour, or a week. It was all the same to Charlie. Their eyes wandered back and forth between each other. Their mouths moved, but Charlie didn’t hear what was being said. He only thought of Vanessa and how he couldn’t get to her.

Charlie’s mom broke the silence. “When will you grow up?” she shouted. “Charles Grimm, this isn’t one of your little games. This is serious.”

Vanessa’s mother sobbed uncontrollably, consoled by Vanessa’s father.

Officer Ron jogged up the steps. “I’ll call in the missing person report. We’ll get an Amber Alert out as soon as possible.”

Charlie’s mom helped Vanessa’s parents up the steps.

Charlie’s father approached in large steps. His chest puffed out and his head pulled back. He pointed a finger at Charlie, wagging it back and forth. “I want you to go upstairs and head to bed right now,” he commanded. “We’ll discuss this in the morning.”

Charlie flared out his arms before smacking the sides of his legs. “But Dad, I’m telling you the truth.” His voice cracked, pleading for anyone to believe him.

“I don’t want to hear it. Playtime is over. You’re thirteen. This is serious. Upstairs. Now!”

“But, Dad . . .” Charlie said.

“You’re done,” Charle’s dad scolded. “You need to grow up.”

Charlie slumped his head, curling in his lips. His fingers dragged across the mirror, hoping one final touch would activate it.

There was nothing. Only his defeated, dejected reflection.

Charlie sniffled, fighting the urge to bawl his eyes out as he climbed the steps. He knew where his friend was. Trapped in a magical realm. Hopefully safe. She must be scared. Maybe something happened on her end. Maybe she tried to get back and couldn’t?

Charlie’s dad pulled on the drawstring, shrouding the basement in darkness.

In that moment, Charlie vowed to never stop trying. To never let her down.

On that night, a girl vanished, and a young boy vowed to wait for her.

She survived the war.

Coming home was only the beginning.

Former Army CID agent 𝗞𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗛𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 returned with scars, medals—and no memory of how she escaped captivity.

Peace didn’t follow her back to Arkansas.

When a wounded German Shepherd is abandoned on her land, Kate refuses to walk away.

Ruger wasn’t trained to save her life.
𝗛𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝗱 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝘆𝘄𝗮𝘆.

Together, Kate and Ruger take on the cases no one else will touch—murders buried by silence, betrayals that destroy families, and truths that refuse to stay buried.

What begins as survival becomes trust.
And trust becomes a bond worth fighting for.

𝑺𝒊𝒙 𝒃𝒐𝒐𝒌𝒔. 𝑶𝒏𝒆 𝒘𝒂𝒓𝒓𝒊𝒐𝒓. 𝑶𝒏𝒆 𝒅𝒐𝒈. 𝑬𝒏𝒅𝒍𝒆𝒔𝒔 𝒅𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒆𝒓.

🔥 Written by a former US Navy lieutenant

𝗜’𝗺 𝗮 𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗳𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝘆 𝘀𝗶𝗹𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗳𝗼𝘅 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 “𝗻𝗼 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗵𝗶𝗺” 𝗿𝘂𝗹𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝗳𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗲𝘀.

Jason Wolfe is a grieving widower whose recluse vibe is threatening his media empire.

His team pushes him to enter a televised Christmas couples competition to prove he's "still human".
The snag? He needs a girlfriend.
So I take the role to keep him and his son safe, not to curl up in his bed.

On cue, I take his hand and smile like I’m his.
His thumb finds the pulse at my wrist and circles like it belongs there.

Our kisses don’t stop at “cut,” and one night… neither do we.
We stop pretending it ends when the cameras do.

Then an alarm blares, the crowd surges, and I throw myself in front of Jason and his son, getting them to safety on instinct.

The cameras catch my actions, and the truth leaks.
Fake girlfriend. Reckless father.

We’re finally real but someone’s made us a scandal.
Now we must fight for us, for our love… or risk losing our chance at forever.

❤️ Find out what happens!

𝗨𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗱𝗼𝗱𝗴𝗲 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗮𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗺𝘆 𝘀𝗼𝗻’𝘀 𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗺𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗴𝗶𝗿𝗹𝗳𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗱.

I ask Ronni Yates to play my girlfriend for ten days. 
She agrees with bulletproof rules and romance that ends at “cut.”

On duty, she’s boots and tactical calm. 
On camera, she’s a Bond girl who’d actually take the shot. 

In snowy Aspenvale, we sell the romance. 

She takes my hand and smiles like she’s mine. 
My thumb finds the pulse at her wrist and circles like it belongs there. 
The kisses don’t stop at “cut,” and one night… neither do we.

We box it up fast. Aspenvale stays in Aspenvale.

Until an alarm screams and the crowd surges. 
Ronni shields my son with her body—and I’m done pretending she’s just a bodyguard.

My billions. The rules. The age gap. 
None of it matters in the instant I know I've fallen for her.

Then a saboteur leaks the truth and the headlines shift. 
Fake couple. Reckless father. 
My board wants damage control, and it starts with her.

If I choose control, I lose her.
If I choose her, I risk losing everything I’ve built.

❤️ Find out what happens!

body.text:
Ambik Ilmu dari Permata Yang Hilang ni.

Paksu dah lama mengurut dekat 17 tahun dah. Macam-macam jenis pele paksu pegang. Bila pegang tu kadang-kadang tau dah masalah apa. 

Yang mai kat paksu ni bukan orang tua. La ni, ramai orang tua. Yang baru kahwin ada, yang tak kahwin lagi pun ada.

Kadang-kadang baru cuit sikit, baru masuk sikit dah muntah. Kena tunggu 15 minit bagi dia naik balik. Kadang-kadang tak naik dah dia sambung tidur. Kesian kat isteri.

.

Paksu rasa mungkin sbb la ni teknologi, masa muda rajin tengok blue dan buat guna tangan sendiri..tu yang jadi takleh tahan lama tu.

Ada juga sebab fktor makanan, suka minum air ais atau makan mknan berminyak.

Kena tahu kalau ada kencing manis atau kolestrol dia mmg akan effect performance kita.

.

Bila ada kolestrol dgn kencing manis..saluran darah jadi sempit..jadi aliran darah tu tak mengalir cantik.. 

Kita punya pele ni, takda tulang..dia keraih sebab aliran darah la rangsang dia untuk stim.. bila darah tak mengalir cantik mcm mana la dia nak keraih.

Tu yg kadang2 time mendayung pun lembik..pasai aliran darah tak cantik..

.

Paksu bagi tips. Amalkan 3 herba ni.

1 . Ubijaga - Ubijaga ni jadi amalan orang asli dan melayu khas utk selesaikan masalah pele cepat muntah.Dia juga merawat kencing manis punca pele jadi lembik.
2. Tongkat Ali 3 warna (putih, hitam, merah) - jgn ambik yang biasa. Amalkan yg 3 warna ni. Untuk kuatkan batang pele.
3. Delima & madu - Untuk tambah tenaga lelaki.

.

Kalau rasa susah nak amalkan atau cari herba ni jangan risau. Paksu tolong hanpa.

Paksu nak rekomen minuman herba nama dia Natura Plus.
Dalam Natura Plus ni ada ubi jaga ni, ashwagandha, tongkat ali tiga, delima, kurma dengan madu.

Ramuan ni dah cukup untuk selesaikan 2 masalah. Dia turunkan kolestrol, stabilkan bacaan gula. Dalam masa yang sama boleh buat pele keraih dan perform. 

Lepas tu dia siap letak delima kurma dengan madu untuk tenaga..pele keraih tp tenaga takdak pun tak guna kan.

.
Yang Natura Plus ni lulus labtest report dari Halal Verification & Consultation Lab (Halvec) lagi tau.. bukan saja2 paksu nak rekomen. Paksu dah daftar dengan KKM siap dah.

.

Nak order macam mana? order kat sini :
https://revbioherb.com/
https://revbioherb.com/
https://revbioherb.com/

p/s : Masa ikhtiar dengan Natura Plus ni, try amalkan posisi dalam gambar ni.  Sebab isteri cepat sampai inzal, kita pulak boleh sama-sama kontrol game. Kena kerjasama supaya sama-sama menang.

Boleh COD, beli 2 dapat ebook Permata Yang Hilang.
Beli 3 paksu bagi extra ebook utk posisi bahagiakan isteri.

body.text:
✨ GIÁO TRÌNH NÀO BÁM SÁT TIÊU CHUẨN HSK 3.0 ĐẦU TIÊN?

Bạn đang tìm kiếm một bộ giáo trình tiếng Trung có thể vừa giúp bạn xây dựng nền tảng toàn diện, vừa bám sát và hỗ trợ tối đa cho kỳ thi HSK format mới nhất (3.0)? Câu trả lời chính là MSUTONG - bộ giáo trình TIÊN PHONG được biên soạn chuyên sâu theo Tiêu chuẩn HSK 3.0 ngay từ đầu.

📚 Vì sao MSUTONG là "sinh ra dành cho HSK 3.0"?
Thiết kế cấu trúc "hai trong một": Bộ 12 cuốn được chia rõ ràng thành Sơ (HSK 1-3), Trung (HSK 4), Cao cấp (HSK 5), hoàn toàn tương ứng với các cấp độ HSK 3.0. Lượng chữ Hán, từ vựng và điểm ngữ pháp trong mỗi cấp độ đều BAO PHỦ & VƯỢT TRỘI so với yêu cầu của tiêu chuẩn mới, đảm bảo bạn học đến đâu, vững kiến thức thi HSK đến đó.

👨Hạt nhân học thuật đỉnh cao: Chủ biên là GS. Ngô Trung Vĩ (ĐH Phúc Đán) – chuyên gia uy tín trực tiếp tham gia xây dựng các tiêu chuẩn của Trung tâm Hợp tác Giao lưu Ngôn ngữ Trung Quốc thế giới (语合中心), định hình Khung tiêu chuẩn HSK 3.0 toàn cầu từ trước 2021. Sự am hiểu sâu sắc này được tích hợp trọn vẹn vào từng trang sách MSUTONG.

📊 Hiệu quả thực tế đã được kiểm chứng: Theo khảo sát, trên 70% học viên chọn MSUTONG để ôn thi HSK cảm thấy HÀI LÒNG vì giáo trình đáp ứng hoàn toàn mục tiêu của họ. Tỷ lệ này đồng đều ở cả 3 cấp độ, chứng tỏ sự hiệu quả xuyên suốt.

🧠 MSUTONG không chỉ giúp bạn THI tốt, mà còn DÙNG tốt tiếng Trung với các tiêu chí vừa thỏa mãn HSK 3.0 vừa đáp ứng đúng yêu cầu công việc: 
- Bài tập "nhiệm vụ" giả lập: Giúp bạn vận dụng ngôn ngữ linh hoạt trong các tình huống đời sống, công việc, không chỉ học vẹt.
- Rèn luyện tư duy đoạn văn: Phát triển khả năng diễn đạt mạch lạc, tự nhiên.
- Nội dung hiện đại, thiết thực: Cập nhật chủ đề và phong cách ngôn ngữ của giới trẻ Trung Quốc và quốc tế.
